html:
The Kingdom of Kashmir was the Hindu and Buddhist kingdom of the Kashmir Valley in the western Himalaya. The map shows it around 700, under the Karkota dynasty, which ruled from about 625 to 855.

The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang spent about two years studying in Kashmir around 631, when it was a famous Buddhist centre. The best known Karkota king, Lalitaditya Muktapida, who ruled in the first half of the 700s, led campaigns across northern India and built the great sun temple at Martand. The Utpala dynasty that followed drained marshes and built irrigation works.

Most of what we know comes from the Rajatarangini, a verse history of Kashmir's kings written by Kalhana in 1148 to 1149. Hindu kings ruled until 1339, when Shah Mir founded a Muslim sultanate, the Shah Mir dynasty.
